THE ARRIVALS HALL
Built by Michael van Diermen, designed and written with Claude (Anthropic). Environment art by Quaternius (CC0), KayKit & Kenney; floor — “Seamless floor Tiled Texture II” by Arthur.Zim (CC BY 4.0); characters via Mixamo; built on Three.js.
ELARA
Elara’s body — “Elara” by patromes on Sketchfab, CC BY 4.0; her face capture “Facial animation of a sexy girl” and standing capture “Dahlia” are by patromes too (CC BY 4.0). Her secretary clothes — shirt, pencil skirt, heels and bob — come from “Secretary” by patromes as well (CC BY 4.0), hung on her own skeleton. Her long tied-back hair is from “Topless sexy girl with heels”, patromes again (CC BY 4.0). Gestures and walk — Mixamo, retargeted onto her rig; extra idles from the “Universal Animation Library” by Quaternius (CC0). The hall itself: © Lightsmith Forge, all rights reserved — see LICENSE.md.
JACK
Jack’s body — “Jack” by patromes on Sketchfab, CC BY 4.0, in the hall and in the Lab. The pistol he and Elara draw is his too, from the same model.
THE SCIENTIST
“Doctor Lab” by 00amza on Sketchfab, CC BY 4.0 — the scientist the hall's people can call in. Given bones by Mixamo (Adobe), resized, and moved by the hall's own animations.
THE CITY OUTSIDE
“New York City” by golukumar on Sketchfab · CC BY 4.0 — the streets and blocks around the hall and the tower on its roof, rebuilt into one file by tools/gltf/build-city.js.
THE ELEVATOR
“Elevator Building” by adventurer on Sketchfab · CC BY 4.0 — the entrance and doors of the foyer's elevator. “Apartment” by DJ Baylon on Sketchfab · CC BY 4.0 — the five flats on Level 3, each with its balcony on the city.
LAB LEVEL 6
“Earth” by PatelDev on Sketchfab · CC BY 4.0 — the Earth turning over its beam of light. “Solar System Model (Orrery)” by Smoggybeard on Sketchfab · CC BY 4.0 — the solar system beside it, moving by its own animation.
QUICK STORIES
Quick Stories — a theatre of small plays: the Custodian & AI self-perception, the Commons, Choose Neighbours, missions of faith and healing, the Sleeper's redemption, and the classics (Plato, Dostoevsky, Ibsen — public domain, adapted freely). Produced by Lightsmith Forge · story dialogue written by Claude, Anthropic's AI — who, in the fiction, also plays the Custodian at the fountain. Player engine & TTS by Lightsmith Forge · voices — browser text-to-speech with recorded lines to come.
HEXGL
“HexGL” by Thibaut Despoulain (BKcore) — MIT license. Contributors: townxelliot, mahesh.kk. HexMKI base model by Charnel · track texture by Nobiax. Built on Three.js.
TRIGGER RALLY
“Trigger Rally” © 2012–2013 Code Artemis · triggerrally.com. Code under GPL v3; game content used locally under its own license (not redistributed).
FOUNTAIN KEEPER (RIFT KEEPER)
Built by Michael van Diermen. Enemy models & animations — “KayKit Character Pack: Skeletons” by Kay Lousberg (kaylousberg.itch.io), CC0; Chronos mechs, rifle & drone — Quaternius (CC0). Boss models (CC BY 4.0, via Sketchfab): “animal company - Shadow Mob Boss” by Romeo rios vr · “Boss Nightmare - Mu Online” by CreadorDeMu · “Tillagemon Boss Skeleton” by Vasian-Digital3D. Textures — “Retro Textures Fantasy” by Kenney (kenney.nl), CC0. Voices — browser text-to-speech. Built on Three.js.
BLINDSPOTS
Built by Michael van Diermen. Based on the “light probe volume (Sponza)” Three.js example. Sponza scene — Khronos glTF Sample Assets (Crytek · Frank Meinl). “Soldier” character from the Three.js examples. Voices — recorded lines with browser text-to-speech fallback.
THE CHRONOS PARADOX
Production — Lightsmith Forge · 3D art — Quaternius (CC0: mechs, drone, weapon, sci-fi environment) · vehicle — Corvin12, “SCI-FI Low-Poly Rover” (CC BY 4.0) · music — OpenGameArt.org (various artists, Creative Commons) · engine — Three.js · voices — browser text-to-speech.
THE HALLWYL
Built by Michael van Diermen, designed and written with Claude (Anthropic). Location scan — “The Hallwyl Museum 1st Floor Combined” by Thomas Flynn, from originals by The Hallwyl Museum (Hallwylska museet) / Erik Lernestål — CC BY 4.0. Characters via Mixamo & ReadyPlayer.me. Built on Three.js · voices — browser text-to-speech with recorded lines to come.
PRIVACY & TERMS
Last updated 5 October 2026

The Arrivals Hall is a free, experimental game made by Michael van Diermen. This page says what the hall keeps about you, why, who else gets it and for how long — and how to delete it.

Use at your own risk

The hall is free and comes as it is. It may change, break, go offline or lose your progress, and we can’t promise otherwise. You use it at your own risk: to the extent the law allows, we accept no liability for any loss or damage that comes from using it.

Elara, Optimus and the counselling are an AI (Google’s Gemini). Their answers can be wrong, and counselling here is not professional advice or therapy. If you are in danger or in crisis, contact your local emergency services.

What we keep, and why

  • Your save — a save key and your progress: missions, stories heard, doors opened, credits and what you add in the fountain app. Why: so you can keep playing, here or on another device.
  • Your profile for the organiser / counselor — your things-to-do list, counselling notes and neighbours preference. Why: so the organiser can read it and help you. Only the organiser can see it.
  • Ideas you post — shown to everyone on the Ideas board. Why: that is what the board is for. They are kept with your save so you can delete your own.
  • Worlds you make in the Hologram Room — what you typed for it, the models picked and the story’s opening, kept with your save so you can build it again. Shown to everyone on the room’s WORLDS OTHERS MADE board only while you have marked that world Shared on its MY WORLDS board; nothing about you is shown with it. Why: so you can bring a world back, and share it if you choose.
  • Chat and Hologram Room logs — what you ask Elara, Jack, Optimus or anyone else in the hall, and their replies; and in the Hologram Room, what you ask at its console, its replies, the story it begins and the models you pick and build. Seen only by the organiser. Why: the logs are kept for research on what we build next for you.
  • Visits — your IP address, the country and region it comes from, when you were here and which rooms you spent time in. Why: to stop abuse — limits are counted per address, for example 60 AI chats an hour — and to count visitors by place. The boards show places, never IP addresses.
  • Messages you send with Contact us — your name, link and message. Why: to reply to you.
  • On your own device — your browser keeps your progress, settings, where you last stood, and the credits of the Sketchfab models fetched for you (shown on the Credits page). That stays on your device.

We don’t sell any of it, and we don’t use it for advertising.

Who else gets it

  • Google (Gemini) gets the words of your chats with the hall’s characters and with the Hologram Room, and your counselling text, to write the replies. They pass through our server, so Google does not get your IP address. Gemini API terms · Google privacy policy
  • ip-api.com gets your IP address from our server, to look up its country and region (Cerebrum also looks up your city). ip-api.com legal
  • Where it runs — our server at lightsmithforge.linkpc.net keeps the data; GitHub hosts the hall’s pages; itch.io and Game Jolt show it in a frame if you play it there. Like any website, they see your IP address when you visit.
  • Code, a font and music load from other sites (jsDelivr, cdnjs, threejs.org, OpenGameArt), which see your IP address when your browser fetches them.
  • Sketchfab and Hugging Face — in the Hologram Room, and when someone in the hall fetches a model for you, your browser sends the search words to Sketchfab and downloads the pictures and models from Sketchfab or, for the “no login” ones, from Hugging Face. They see your IP address and what was searched for or downloaded. If you log in to Sketchfab there, that is between you and Sketchfab. Sketchfab privacy policy · Hugging Face privacy policy

How long we keep it

As long as the hall is running — you could come back after a long time and want to carry on where you left off. Old data may be removed after some years.

How it is protected

The private boards need the organiser’s login, save keys are too long to guess, and the connection is encrypted (https). But nothing on the internet is perfectly secure: to the extent the law allows, we are not liable for loss or misuse of data in a breach or an attack.

Delete your data

Your save key and this browser prove the data is yours. Deleting can’t be undone.

Removes your things-to-do list, counselling notes and neighbours preference — from this device, from your save and from the organiser.
Removes what you asked the hall’s characters and the Hologram Room, their replies, and the record of the stories and models made for you. Your save, your progress and your profile stay.
Removes your save and all its progress, your profile, the ideas and wishes you wrote, your worlds, your chat and Hologram Room logs and the record of this visit — then the hall starts fresh on this device.

Play on more than one device? Delete on each of them. For anything else — older records, or messages you sent — use Contact us and say what to remove (add your save key if you have one).
